questions.question: The product method which is used to calculate the aggregate annual value of goods and services produced is also called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Value added method**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Value Added Method: **
 
• This approach to calculating the aggregate annual value of goods and services produced in an economy, often referred to in calculating GDP, is also known as the value added method or the production method.
 
• This method includes the total of all gross value added by all resident producer units in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income Method:**

 
 
• This is another method of **measuring GDP, **which is based on the total income earned by **all households, firms, and the government.**
 
• It includes **wages and salaries, rents, interest, profits, and miscellaneous income** earned by the residents of the country during the year.
 
• It doesn't consider transfer payments such as **pensions, unemployment benefits, or welfare payments because these are not earned in return for goods or services produced.**
 
 
 
• **Depreciation Method:**
 
 
• This method isn't directly used to **calculate GDP or aggregate value of goods and services.**
 
• Depreciation refers to the** decrease in the value of physical capital—from equipment to buildings—as it is used over time and wear and tear takes place.**
 
• However, depreciation is accounted into **Net Domestic Product (NDP)**, which is GDP minus depreciation on a country's capital goods.
 
 
 
• **Expenditure Method: **
 
 
• This is one of the **three** **chief methods of calculating GDP**.
 
• It measures the total spending on all final goods and services **(consumption expenditure, investment, government spending, and net exports) produced within a country within a specified period of time.**
 
• It includes consumer spending on **goods and services, government spending, capital investments made by businesses, and net exports (exports minus imports).**

questions.question: "Ambubachi Mela" is held in which place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guwahati**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ambubachi Mela** is held annually at the **Kamakhya Temple** in **Guwahati, Assam, India**.
 
• It is a** four-day festival** to mark the menstruation of the **Goddess Kamakhya, believed to be the earth's period of menstruation.**
 
• During this time the temple remains closed for three days, and it is believed that the **earth becomes unclean**.
 
• On the fourth day, **the temple reopens and a large number of devotees visit to receive prasad (holy offering).​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pune: **

 
 
• The city of Pune is famous for** the Osho International Meditation Resort, hence, the Osho Festival of Music and Meditation attracts many visitors from around the world.**
 
• Pune also hosts the **Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Festival, one of the largest Indian Classical music festivals in India.**
 
 
 
• **Patna: **
 
 
• **The city of Patna** in** Bihar** is famous for** the Chhath Puja, an ancient Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun God Surya.**
 
• **The Chhath Puja** involves **rigorous rituals, including fasting and standing in water for long periods.**
 
 
 
• **Lucknow**:
 
 
• **Lucknow,** the capital city of** Uttar Pradesh,** is known for the **Muharram festival, which is observed to mourn the death of Imam Hussain, the grandson of Prophet Mohammed.**
 
• The city is famous for the elaborate processions carried out during **Muharram**.
 
• It also hosts **Lucknow Mahotsav,** an annual event** showcasing arts, crafts, and the rich cultural heritage of Lucknow.**

questions.question: Stand Up India scheme aims at supporting entrepreneurship to _______ community of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scheduled Caste**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Stand Up India scheme aims to **support entrepreneurship among women, Scheduled Castes (SC), and Scheduled Tribes (ST).**
 
• The goal is to enable these underserved sectors of the population to start new enterprises and become economically self-sufficient.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Business Person:**

 
 
• This term generally refers to any individual who owns and operates a business.
 
• These are individuals who undertake the **financial risk of the initiation, operation, and management of a business.**
 
 
 
• **Construction Workers: **
 
 
• This group refers to **manual laborers who work in construction.**
 
• They perform tasks involving **physical labor at construction sites and may operate hand and power tools of all types.**
 
 
 
• **Below Poverty Line (BPL):**
 
 
• This term refers to a benchmark set by the government of India to identify economically disadvantaged people who need government assistance.
 
• The BPL benchmark is based on various parameters including **income, size of land holdings, and literacy rate.**
 
• According to **India's Development Goals, people below the poverty line should be supported with social security and welfare programs.**

questions.question: How many field players are in a football team?
questions.solution:
the correct answer is __**11**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a game of football (soccer), there are **11 field players on each team.**
 
• **The Field**:
 
 
• The game is played on a rectangular field with a goal at each end.
 
• The dimensions of the field can vary but are roughly 100 to 130 yards long and 50 to 100 yards wide.
 
 
 
• **Objective: **The objective of the game is to score by moving the ball beyond the goal line into the opposing goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Game Duration:**

 
 
• The standard game duration is 90 minutes, divided into two halves of 45 minutes each, with a 15-minute halftime break.
 
 
 
• **Offside Rule:**
 
 
• A player is considered offside if they are closer to the opposing team's goal than both the ball and the second-last opponent when the ball is played to them.
 
 
 
• **Fouls and Misconduct:**
 
 
• Certain actions are considered fouls, such as hitting, tripping, pushing, or holding an opponent.
 
• Unfair behavior can result in free kicks or penalty kicks for the opposing team.
 
• If a player commits a serious foul, they may be given a yellow card (warning) or a red card (dismissal from the game).
 
 
 
• **Positioning: **
 
 
• The positions of the players can vary depending on the strategy employed by the coach.
 
• However, basic positions include defenders, midfielders, forwards, and the goalkeeper.
 
 
 
• **Winning:**
 
 
• The team with the most goals at the end of the game wins.
 
• If the game ends in a tie, it may go into extra time or penalty shootout, depending on the format of the competition.

Oscar Awards:

• It was first broadcast by radio in 1930 and was televised in 1953 for the first time.
 
• It is the oldest worldwide entertainment awards ceremony.

questions.question: Which is the largest continent in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Asia Continent

__
 
• Asia is the world's largest continent, having an area of 44,444,100 km2. 
 
• It covers about one-third of the total land area of the earth.
 
• The continent lies in the Eastern Hemisphere.
 
• The Tropic of Cancer passes through this continent.
 
• Asia is separated from Europe by the Ural mountains on the west.
 
• It covers 8.8% of the Earth’s total surface area with a population of 4.4 billion which is 60 % of the world’s total population.
 
• It is a continent of contrast in relief, temperature, vegetation, and people also.
 
• Asia is to the east of the Suez Canal, the Ural River, and the Ural Mountains, and south of the Caucasus Mountains and the Caspian and Black Seas.
 
• It is bounded on the east by the Pacific Ocean, on the south by the Indian Ocean, and on the north by the Arctic Ocean.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ab904072eb623bb22811859e3637cde373ee691d2933c926355e34d9da99384.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are seven major continents. These are separated by large water bodies.
 
• These continents are – Asia, Europe, Africa, North America, South America, Australia, and Antarctica.
 
• The greater part of the landmass lies in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• The combined landmass of Europe and Asia is called Eurasia (Europe + Asia).

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Practice of "sati" was banned in India in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1829__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1829__, the practice of Sati was banned.
 
• Sati was a practice among Hindu communities where a recently widowed woman, either voluntarily or by force, immolates herself on her deceased husband's pyre.
 __
 
• Raja Rammohan Roy, the great Hindu reformer from Bengal fought many social evils prevalent in the Hindu society of Bengal and Sati pratha was one of the chief ones.
 
• Lord William Bentinck became the Governor-General of India in 1828.
 
• He helped Raja Rammohan Roy to suppress many prevalent social evils like Sati, polygamy, child marriage and female infanticide.
 
• The Bengal Sati Regulation which banned the Sati practice in all jurisdictions of British India was passed on 4 December 1829 by the then Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Lord William Bentinck -

 
 
• He was appointed the Governor of Madras in 1803. 
 
• He assumed the office of the Governor-General in 1828. 
 
• As Governor-General, Bentinck had initiated an era of progress and reforms.
 
• He became the first governor-general of India (due to the provision in the Charter Act of 1833). 
 
• William Bentinck adopted a policy of non-intervention and non-aggression with Indian states.
 
• In the judicial department, he abolished the provincial courts of appeal established by Cornwallis.

questions.question: Udaipur was founded by ______ after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in 1568.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Udai Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rana Udai Singh**

 
 
• Udaipur was founded by Maharana Udai Singh after the fall of Chittor to Akbar in **1568**.
 
• Rana Udai Singh was the ruler of the kingdom of Mewar in present-day** Rajasthan,** India.
 
• When the Mughal emperor Akbar seized Chittor, which was then the **capital of Mewar**, Udai Singh moved his capital to a more secure location.
 
• As per the advice of a hermit, he chose the area around **Lake Pichola** for his new capital, which was named after him as Udaipur.
 
• Unlike most other Rajput kingdoms, Mewar continued to resist the Mughals, under the leadership of several generations of **Sisodia Rajputs**.
 
• Rana Udai Singh and his successors, notably **Maharana Pratap Singh**, are remembered as national heroes in India for their resistance to the Mughals, especially Akbar.
 
• The city of Udaipur is celebrated for its lake-studded, romantic setting and sweeping architectural grandeur, including magnificent palaces such as the **City Palace, Lake Palace, and Jag Mandi**r.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Name
 Information
 
 
 
 

 **Man Singh**
 Man Singh (1540-1614) was the Rajput Raja of Amer (Jaipur), a state in Rajasthan, India. He was a trusted general in the court of the Mughal emperor Akbar, who included him among his 'navaratnas', or nine gems. Man Singh helped Akbar consolidate his empire through his military and diplomatic skills.
 
 

 **Raja Bharmal**
 Raja Bharmal of Amber (also in Rajasthan) was the first Rajput ruler to marry his daughter, Harkha Bai (later known as Jodha Bai or Mariam-uz-Zamani), to a Mughal - Emperor Akbar. This alliance was a fundamental turning point which began a tradition of Rajput-Mughal political marriages, aiding the stabilization of relations between the two powers.
 
 

 **Sawai Jai Singh**
 Sawai Jai Singh II (1688-1743) was the founder of Jaipur city, the capital of Rajasthan. An esteemed ruler of the Kachwaha clan of Rajputs, he was also an avid astronomer and built several observatories known as 'Jantar Mantars' in different cities of India. During his reign, architecture, education, and astronomy flourished, leading to significant advancements. Jai Singh's most significant achievement was the construction of Jaipur, which was designed according to the principles of Vastu Shastra and Shilpa Shastra, becoming one of the earliest examples of a planned city in India.

questions.question: Which of the following material is a conductor of electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Conductivity: The measure of the ease at which an electric charge can pass through a material is called electrical conductivity.
 
• Conductor: The material which has high conductivity is called the conductor.
 
• Non-conductor: The material which has very low conductivity is called non-conductor.
 
• Metal has high conductivity and non-metal has very low conductivity
 
• Electrical Conductivity is the evaluation of a material's ability to allow the transport of an electric charge.
 
• Silver is by far the most electrically conductive metal on earth. Since silver has only one valence electron which is free to move around with little resistance, it has great electrical and thermal conductivity.
 
• After silver, copper is the second most electrically conductive metal. Gold and Aluminium are other metals which are good conductors of electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Material
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Glass
 Glass is a non-crystalline amorphous solid that often appears and has widespread practical, technological, and decorative applications. Its uses include window panes, drinkware, and optoelectronics. Its most significant characteristics include transparency, brittleness, hardness, and resistance to chemical attack.
 
 

 Mica
 Mica is a group of silicate minerals that are widely distributed in different types of rock. Mica has a crystalline structure that allows it to be split into thin sheets. These sheets are flexible, heat-resistant, and electrically insulating, making mica useful in the electronics and electrical industries, and in the manufacturing of cosmetics.
 
 

 Ebonite
 Ebonite is a type of hard rubber, also known as vulcanite or hard vulcanized rubber. It's made by treating rubber with sulfur at high temperatures, a process known as vulcanization. The resulting material is hard and black, resembling ebony, which gives it its name. Ebonite has high electrical resistance and chemical stability, making it appropriate for applications like electrical insulators and bowling balls. It is also historically used for wind musical instruments like clarinets and mouthpieces of other wind instruments because of its excellent machining properties.

questions.question: Which among the following dance forms of India is associated with Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalbelia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalbelia**

 
 
• Kalbelia or kalbeliya dance form is associated with a Rajasthani tribe of the same name.
 
• Kalbeliya dance was included in UNESCO’s list of the Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.
 
• It is performed by the women of the Kalbeliya community.
 
• Kalbeliya dancer's clothes are flowing black skirts mixed in red and black hues and embroidered in unique patterns.
 
• Kalbeliya dance has traditional musical instruments known as Poongi.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Dance Form
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Odissi
 Originated from the Eastern Indian state of Odisha, Odissi is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India. It is characterized by its graceful and expressional performance. The dance is a blend of Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (dance with emotions) and Natya (dramatic representation). Odissi is typically accompanied by musicians, where the dancer's motions express the song's narrative and emotions.
 
 

 Bharatanatyam
 Bharatanatyam is a classical Indian dance form originating from Tamil Nadu. This dance form is known for its grace, elegance, purity, tenderness, expression and sculpturesque poses. Bharatanatyam generally follows the theoretical framework outlined in the Natya Shastra, an ancient text for theater and performance arts. The dance is highly symbolic and includes gestures (mudras) that communicate stories from Indian mythology and spiritual ideas.
 
 

 Kathakali
 Kathakali is a major form of classical Indian dance originating in the Indian state of Kerala. It is a performance art that combines dancing, acting, vocal music, percussion, costumes and make-up. Kathakali's stories are taken from the Indian epics and Puranas, and the performance is characterized by its dramatic and elaborate costumes and makeup, as well as the detailed gestures, expressions and dance movements.

__
 
• Genghis Khan was the founder of the Mongol Empire in 1206 and launched military campaigns in China and Central Asia.

 
 
• ​The Mongols were a nomadic tribe whole lived between the Ural Mountains and the Gobi Desert in Central Asia who always was at war until their military general, Temujin or also called Genghis Khan united them.
 
 
 
• The Mongols under Genghis Khan invaded Transoxiana in North-East Iran in 1219. Hence option 1 is correct.
 
• Genghis Khan invaded the Jin dynasty in China in 1214 and annexed the Qara Khitai in Central Asia in 1218.
 
• Mongols attacked India between 1221 and 1327 and later by Qaraunas of Mongol origin.

• The battle of Indus was fought between Genghis Khan of the Mongol Empire and Jalal ad-Din Mingburnu of the Khwarezmian Empire in 1221 and resulted in the victory of the Mongols.
 
• In 1227, Ghengis Khan died of illness during his last campaign against Western Xia.

• Population Density rank: 11.

• Female population: 11856728.

• Sex ratio in Rural areas: 882/1000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Sex Ratio in India:

 
 
• Sex ratio is used to describe the number of females per 1000 of males.
 
• Sex ratio is a valuable source for finding the population of women in India and what is the ratio of women to that of men in India.
 
• In the Population Census of 2011, it was revealed that the population ratio in India 2011 is 943 females per 1000 males.
 
• The Sex Ratio 2011 shows an upward trend from the census 2001 data.
 
• Census 2001 revealed that there were 933 females to that of 1000 males.
 
• For decades India has seen a decrease in the sex ratio 2011, but since the last two of the decades, there has been a slight increase in the sex ratio.
 
• Since the last five decades, the sex ratio has been moving from around 930 females to that of 1000 males.

questions.question: Who has the power to interpret the constitution of India?

options.text: Both Supreme court and High courts

questions.solution:
**The correct answer 'Both Supreme court and High courts'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India is one of the very powerful courts anywhere in the world.
 
• The power to interpret the Constitution and entertain judicial review petitions is exercised by the Supreme Court and the High Courts alone and therefore, are referred to as the constitutional courts.
 
• However, it functions within the limitations imposed by the Constitution.
 
• The functions and responsibilities of the Supreme Court are defined by the Constitution.
 
• Article 214 to 231 in part VI of the Constitution deals with the high courts.
 
• The constitution of India provides for a high court for each state
 
• 7th amendment act authorized to establish a common High court for 2 or more state​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Supreme Court has specific jurisdiction or scope of powers.
 
 
• Original: Settles disputes between Union and States and amongst States.
 
• Appellate: Tries appeals from lower courts in Civil, Criminal and Constitutional cases Advisory Advises the President on matters of public importance and law.
 
• Writ: Can issue writs of Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo warranto to protect the Fundamental Rights of the individual.
 
• Special Powers: Can grant special leave to an appeal from any judgement or matter passed by any court in the territory of India.
